newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk army says decisions taken in Islamist dispute.
newsitem.headline: Turk army says decisions taken in Islamist dispute.

text.p: Turkey's secularist army, locked in a war of attrition with the Islamist-led government, on Monday announced it had taken the "necessary decisions" to deal with suspected Moslem activists in its ranks.

"The discipline and moral position of some members of the Turkish armed forces was evaluated and the necessary decisions were taken," the NTV television station quoted a military statement as saying after a marathon meeting of top brass.
Military officials declined to comment on the statement, which gave no details of the decisions taken.

It came after a six-hour meeting of the Supreme Military Council closely watched by the political establishment and financial markets for signs of a final break between the generals and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
The top brass had been expected to demand that Erbakan approve the expulsion from the army of officers suspected of Islamist tendencies.
Newspapers had said that about 100 officers and non-commissioned officers, most of them accused of being Islamists, were to be drummed out of the army at Monday's meeting.
Months of army demands that Erbakan curb a rise in Islamist sentiment has exposed serious cracks in the coalition government.
Four MPs from the alliance's True Path Party secularist wing have resigned since Friday, leaving the government with a majority on paper of only one in the 550-seat parliament.
